q: Two polarising films are crossed, so no light comes through them. A third film whose transmission axis is at an angle of $45^\circ$ to both is slid between them. Why does light start to come through again?
a: After the first film the light is polarised along its transmission axis. The middle film lets part of it through, and after it the light is polarised at an angle of $45^\circ$. This oscillation also has a component along the transmission axis of the last film, so part of the light gets through the last film too. Without the middle film the oscillation reaching the last film is perpendicular to its transmission axis, and no light gets through.

q: A phone display looks bright through polarised sunglasses, but when the phone is turned by $90^\circ$, the display turns almost black. Why?
a: There is a polarising film on the surface of the display, so the light of the display is polarised. When the direction of polarisation of the display is parallel to the transmission axis of the glasses, the light passes through. When the phone is turned by $90^\circ$, the directions are crossed, and almost no light passes through crossed polarisers.
